newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's R.Unicbank Q1 profit down, lendings up.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's R.Unicbank Q1 profit down, lendings up.

text.p: Hungary's Raiffeisen Unicbank Rt on Tuesday reported lower year on year profits for the first quarter of 1997 but its expansion continued, boosting its balance sheet total, a bank official said.

The bank, which belongs to Austria's RZB group, reported a profit before tax and provisions of 1.719 billion forints for the first three months of 1997, down from 1.864 billion in the same three months of 1996.
"The bank's business expansion continued in the first quarter with the balance sheet total...and corporate loans growing," Deputy General Director Ivan Gara told a news conference.
The bank's balance sheet total grew to 130.6 billion forints from 82.759 billion at the end of March 1996. Corporate loans rose to 88.38 billion from 60.443 billion.

"We've tried for long to boost our foreign currency lendings which grew only slowly in the past two years, now a growth began on this area within the bank's portfolio," Gara said. "Still better, medium-term lending also began to grow."
The bank's provisions stood at 230 million forints at the end of the quarter, well down from 579 million at end of March 1996, and were unchanged from the end of the year.
